fullPassage:
The Mind of an Octopus

Here is an animal with poison like a snake, a hard and pointed mouth like a bird, and ink like a pen. It can weigh as much as an adult human and stretch as long as a car. Yet it can put its boneless body through a hole the size of an orange. It can change color and shape, and it can taste with its skin. This animal is called an octopus.

The octopus looks so alien to the people of the West that it has caused dislike or even horror in them. The dislike or horror helped create the image of an octopus as an evil creature living in the deep sea. For example, the Kraken, a sea monster in old Icelandic tales, looks just like an enormous octopus. Another example is Ursula, the sea witch featured in the famous tale, The Little Mermaid. To this day, it is difficult for us to imagine that octopuses and humans share any meaningful similarities.

During the past few decades, however, scientists have begun to find more and more similarities between octopuses and humans. One of the most interesting ones is intelligence. Octopuses are smart. The best evidence is their ability to camouflage themselves. An octopus can change its color, pattern, and texture, and the changes are carried out almost instantly. In terms of speed and the diversity of change, no other animal can rival octopuses. Even chameleons can utilize only a handful of fixed patterns.

The main purpose of these changes is to avoid detection by their hunters or their prey. When an octopus encounters its hunter or prey, it must decide very quickly which color, pattern, and texture to choose. Such a decision implies that it has gained sufficient knowledge of the surrounding animals and applies it to survive. To acquire knowledge and apply it for a particular purpose is a sure sign of intelligence.

Another sign of the intelligence of the octopus is its use of tools. In the lab, octopuses use tools to get food rewards. In the wild, they use stones to create walls to protect the entrances to their homes. They use not only stones but anything they can find to protect themselves. The most impressive example of octopuses using tools came in 2009 in Indonesia. A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses more exposed to predators. But it seems that they were willing to take that risk for greater future protection. The scientists who discovered the behavior argue that this is clear evidence of octopuses using tools.

Octopuses' use of tools can be found in their love of toys and puzzles, too. They are curious about new objects, and do not like getting bored. That is why aquariums try to come up with ideas to keep their octopuses busy. Some aquariums hide food inside a big doll and let the octopus break up the toy to get the food. Others offer plastic building blocks for their octopuses to play with.

Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is expanding year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus is that it seems to have feelings. Of course, it is impossible for us to know exactly what they feel, but a few of their changes in skin color seem to be linked to their feelings. For example, a giant Pacific octopus that turns red seems to be excited, while it is white when it is relaxed. An octopus presented with a difficult puzzle often undergoes several rapid changes in color. The octopus seems to be worried that it may not solve the problem.

Few scientists today deny that octopuses are intelligent animals. Perhaps it is time that we stopped thinking of them as alien creatures and acknowledged them as intelligent animals like us. There is still so much we do not know about the octopus. Aren't you curious about what is inside their mind?

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 심해에 사는(living) 사악한 생물이라는 이미지.
det.analysis:
✅ ② lived → living: creature를 수식하는 현재분사가 필요. 능동 의미(살고 있는)이므로 현재분사 living
❌ ① create: helped + 동사원형 적절
❌ ③ like: 전치사 '~처럼' 적절
❌ ④ to imagine: It is difficult for us to V 구문 적절
det.tip: 현재분사 vs 과거분사: 능동(~하는) → -ing, 수동(~된) → -ed. a creature living in ~ = ~에 사는 생물

questions.passage: An octopus can change its color, pattern, and texture, and the changes are carried out almost instantly. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 색깔, 무늬, 질감을 선택할지 매우 빠르게 결정해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ that → which: 'decide which + 명사 + to V' 간접의문문에서 의문형용사 which가 필요. that은 의문형용사로 쓸 수 없음
❌ ① to avoid: 'The purpose is to V' 구문 적절
❌ ② encounters: 주어 'an octopus'(단수)에 맞는 동사
❌ ④ applies: 'it has gained ~ and applies ~' 병렬 구조 적절
det.tip: 의문사 + to V: which color to choose(어떤 색을 선택할지). that은 의문형용사 불가

questions.passage: A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses ①<u>more exposed</u> to predators. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 문어가 도구를 사용하는 명백한 증거.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ used → using: 'evidence of octopuses using tools'에서 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사(using) 구문이 필요. octopuses가 using의 의미상 주어
❌ ① more exposed: 비교급 + 과거분사 적절
❌ ② were willing: be willing to V 적절
❌ ③ who: 선행사 The scientists(사람)를 수식하는 관계대명사 적절
det.tip: evidence of + 동명사: ~하는 증거. 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 옴

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 문어는 서양 사람들에게 너무 낯설어서 ②존경(→ dislike 혐오감) 또는 공포마저 불러일으켰다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② admiration(존경)은 원문 dislike(혐오감)의 반의어로 부적절. horror와 병렬이므로 부정적 감정이 와야 함
❌ ① alien(낯선): 서양 사람들에게 낯설다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ evil(사악한): 심해 사악한 생물 이미지에 적절
❌ ④ similarities(유사점): 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: dislike(혐오감) ↔ admiration(존경). or even horror = 심지어 공포까지

questions.passage: Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is ①<u>expanding</u> year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus is that it seems to have feelings. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 붉은색으로 변한 대왕문어는 ③편안한(→ excited 흥분한) 것처럼 보인다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ relaxed(편안한)는 원문 excited(흥분한)로 교체되어야 함. 붉은색=흥분, 흰색=편안이 원문. 여기서는 두 감정이 뒤바뀜
❌ ① expanding(확장되는): 해마다 확장된다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② linked(연결된): 감정과 연결된다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ rapid(급격한): 급격한 색 변화라는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: excited(흥분한) ↔ relaxed(편안한). 색상-감정 매칭: red=excited, white=relaxed

questions.passage: The main purpose of these changes is to avoid detection by their hunters or their prey. When an octopus encounters its hunter or prey, it must decide very quickly which color, pattern, and texture to choose. Such a decision implies that it has gained sufficient knowledge of the surrounding animals and applies it to survive. To __________ and apply it for a particular purpose is a sure sign of intelligence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 지식을 습득하고 특정 목적을 위해 적용하는 것은 지능의 확실한 표시이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① acquire knowledge(지식을 습득하다): 원문 표현. 앞 문장의 'gained sufficient knowledge'와 연결
❌ ② avoid danger(위험을 피하다): 지능의 정의와 직접 관련 없음
❌ ③ change patterns(패턴을 바꾸다): 위장 행동이지 지능의 정의 아님
❌ ④ protect themselves(자신을 보호하다): 지능의 정의와 직접 관련 없음
det.tip: acquire = gain = obtain (얻다/습득하다). acquire knowledge = 지식을 습득하다

questions.passage: Few scientists today deny that octopuses are intelligent animals. Perhaps it is time that we stopped thinking of them as alien creatures and acknowledged them as intelligent animals like us. There is still so much we do not know about the octopus. Aren't you curious about what is inside __________?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 문어의 마음속에 무엇이 있는지 궁금하지 않은가?
det.analysis:
✅ ④ their mind(그들의 마음): 글 제목 'The Mind of an Octopus'와 연결되는 마무리 질문
❌ ① their shells(그들의 껍질): 문어는 껍질이 없음 (boneless)
❌ ② their habitat(그들의 서식지): 마지막 문장 맥락과 무관
❌ ③ the deep sea(심해): 이미지에 불과하고 마음 탐구가 핵심
det.tip: 글 제목과 마지막 문장의 연결: The Mind of an Octopus → what is inside their mind?

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 문어는 피부로 맛을 느낄 수 있다.

det.korean: 문어는 피부로 맛을 느낄 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 'it can taste with its skin'과 일치
❌ ① 독은 뱀처럼(like a snake), 새처럼은 입
❌ ② 몸무게가 사람만큼(weigh as much as an adult human), 길이가 자동차만큼
❌ ④ boneless(뼈가 없는) 동물
det.tip: 세부 사항 변조 주의: poison=snake, mouth=bird, weight=human, stretch=car

questions.passage: Another sign of the intelligence of the octopus is its use of tools. In the lab, octopuses use tools to get food rewards. In the wild, they use stones to create walls to protect the entrances to their homes. The most impressive example of octopuses using tools came in 2009 in Indonesia. questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 실험실에서 문어는 집을 보호하기 위해 돌을 사용한다.
인도네시아에서 코코넛 껍질을 모으는 문어가 발견되었다.
문어들은 코코넛 껍질을 모래로 씻어 정리했다.

det.korean: 인도네시아에서 코코넛 껍질을 모으는 문어가 발견되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 원문 'A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells'(인도네시아)와 일치
❌ ① 돌로 벽을 만드는 건 야생에서(In the wild), 실험실에서는 먹이 보상용
❌ ③ 모래가 아닌 물(bursts of water)로 씻음
❌ ④ 2009년(not 2019년)
det.tip: 연도/장소/방법 변조 주의: 2009년, 인도네시아, bursts of water(물)

questions.passage: Octopuses' use of tools can be found in their love of toys and puzzles, too. They are curious about new objects, and do not like getting bored. That is why aquariums try to come up with ideas to keep their octopuses busy. Some aquariums hide food inside a big doll and let the octopus break up the toy to get the food. Others offer plastic building blocks for their octopuses to play with.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 수족관에서는 문어를 바쁘게 하기 위한 아이디어를 생각해 낸다.
일부 수족관에서는 큰 인형 안에 먹이를 숨긴다.
모든 수족관에서는 문어에게 플라스틱 블록을 제공한다.

det.korean: 모든 수족관이 아닌 일부(Others) 수족관에서 블록을 제공한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ '모든 수족관'은 원문 'Others(다른 수족관들)'와 불일치. 일부만 해당
❌ ① 'curious about new objects'와 일치
❌ ② 'try to come up with ideas'와 일치
❌ ③ 'hide food inside a big doll'과 일치
det.tip: '모든(all)' vs '일부(some/others)' — 범위 한정 변조 주의

questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 문어의 위장 능력을 통해 본 지능

det.korean: 문어의 위장 능력을 통해 본 지능.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 문어와 인간의 유사점 중 지능, 그 증거로 위장 능력을 설명
❌ ① 해양 생물 전반이 아닌 문어 특정
❌ ③ 카멜레온은 비교 대상일 뿐
❌ ④ 연구 이유가 아닌 발견 내용
det.tip: 주제 = 글의 핵심 주장. camouflage → intelligence

questions.passage: Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is expanding year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus is that it seems to have feelings. Of course, it is impossible for us to know exactly what they feel, but a few of their changes in skin color seem to be linked to their feelings. questions.stem: 위 글에서 필자가 전하고자 하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 문어를 낯선 존재가 아닌 지적인 동물로 인정해야 한다.
문어의 감정에 대한 과학적 연구가 완료되었다.
모든 해양 동물은 인간과 동일한 지능을 가진다.
문어에 대한 연구는 더 이상 필요하지 않다.

det.korean: 문어를 낯선 존재가 아닌 지적인 동물로 인정해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'acknowledged them as intelligent animals like us'가 필자의 핵심 주장
❌ ② 연구가 완료된 것이 아니라 still very limited
❌ ③ '모든 해양 동물'은 과잉 일반화
❌ ④ 'still so much we do not know' → 연구가 더 필요
det.tip: 대의 파악: 마지막 단락에서 필자의 주장/제안이 드러남

questions.passage: A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses more exposed to predators. But it seems that they were <u>willing to take that risk</u> for greater future protection.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 'willing to take that risk'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 포식자와 직접 싸울 준비가 되어 있었다
현재의 위험을 감수하고 미래의 안전을 선택했다
해저에서 더 빠르게 이동하는 방법을 찾았다

det.korean: 현재의 위험을 감수하고 미래의 안전을 선택했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 느리게 걸어야 하는 현재 위험(포식자 노출)을 감수하고 미래 보호(은신처)를 위해 껍질을 운반
❌ ① 포식자와 싸우는 것이 아닌 위험 감수
❌ ② 껍질을 버리지 않고 운반함
❌ ④ 빠르게 이동이 아닌 느리게 이동
det.tip: 함축의미: 표면적 의미(위험 감수) → 내면적 의미(미래 보호를 위한 전략적 판단)

questions.passage: Here is an animal with poison like a snake, a hard and pointed mouth like a bird, and ink like a pen. It can change color and shape, and it can taste with its skin. This animal is called an octopus. The octopus looks so alien to the people of the West that it has caused dislike or even horror in <u>them</u>. The dislike or horror helped create the image of an octopus as an evil creature living in the deep sea.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 서양 사람들에게 혐오감이나 공포를 불러일으켰다. them = the people of the West.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 'caused dislike or even horror in them' — them은 앞의 'the people of the West'를 가리킴
❌ ① octopuses: 문어가 혐오를 느끼는 것이 아님
❌ ③ sea monsters: 아직 언급 전
❌ ④ evil creatures: 아직 언급 전
det.tip: 대명사 지칭: 전치사 in + them → 감정을 느끼는 대상 = 사람들

questions.passage: The most impressive example of octopuses using tools came in 2009 in Indonesia. A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the shells with bursts of water, carried <u>them</u> to a new location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses more exposed to predators.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 껍질을 물로 깨끗이 씻어 새로운 장소로 옮겼다(carried them). them = the shells.

questions.passage:
The Mind of an Octopus

Here is an animal with poison like a snake, a hard and pointed mouth like a bird, and ink like a pen. It can weigh as much as an adult human and stretch as long as a car. Yet it can put its boneless body through a hole the size of an orange. It can change color and shape, and it can taste with its skin. This animal is called an octopus.

The octopus looks so alien to the people of the West that it has caused dislike or even horror in them. The dislike or horror helped create the image of an octopus as an evil creature living in the deep sea. For example, the Kraken, a sea monster in old Icelandic tales, looks just like an enormous octopus. Another example is Ursula, the sea witch featured in the famous tale, The Little Mermaid. To this day, it is difficult for us to imagine that octopuses and humans share any meaningful similarities.

During the past few decades, however, scientists have begun to find more and more similarities between octopuses and humans. One of the most interesting ones is intelligence. Octopuses are smart. The best evidence is their ability to camouflage themselves. An octopus can change its color, pattern, and texture, and the changes are carried out almost instantly. In terms of speed and the diversity of change, no other animal can rival octopuses. Even chameleons can utilize only a handful of fixed patterns.

The main purpose of these changes is to avoid detection by their hunters or their prey. When an octopus encounters its hunter or prey, it must decide very quickly which color, pattern, and texture to choose. Such a decision implies that it has gained sufficient knowledge of the surrounding animals and applies it to survive. To acquire knowledge and apply it for a particular purpose is a sure sign of intelligence.

Another sign of the intelligence of the octopus is its use of tools. In the lab, octopuses use tools to get food rewards. In the wild, they use stones to create walls to protect the entrances to their homes. They use not only stones but anything they can find to protect themselves. The most impressive example of octopuses using tools came in 2009 in Indonesia. A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses more exposed to predators. But it seems that they were willing to take that risk for greater future protection. The scientists who discovered the behavior argue that this is clear evidence of octopuses using tools.

Octopuses' use of tools can be found in their love of toys and puzzles, too. They are curious about new objects, and do not like getting bored. That is why aquariums try to come up with ideas to keep their octopuses busy. Some aquariums hide food inside a big doll and let the octopus break up the toy to get the food. Others offer plastic building blocks for their octopuses to play with.

Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is expanding year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus is that it seems to have feelings. Of course, it is impossible for us to know exactly what they feel, but a few of their changes in skin color seem to be linked to their feelings. For example, a giant Pacific octopus that turns red seems to be excited, while it is white when it is relaxed. An octopus presented with a difficult puzzle often undergoes several rapid changes in color. The octopus seems to be worried that it may not solve the problem.

Few scientists today deny that octopuses are intelligent animals. Perhaps it is time that we stopped thinking of them as alien creatures and acknowledged them as intelligent animals like us. There is still so much we do not know about the octopus. Aren't you curious about what is inside their mind?
